close_reason: Dropped the account_id: Option<&Id> override from search_snippet_get for consistency with every other SessionClient method (commit d6df733). Updated rustdoc to call out the removed override + bead reference; updated README method table; updated tests/search_snippet_smoke_tests.rs to remove the override-specific test and adjust the two surviving tests to the new signature. Session-account binding is still implicitly covered by the two surviving wiremock tests (both assert args[accountId] matches helpers::make_client's session binding). Not canonical-template propagation — search_snippet is mail-spec-specific. Workspace pre-commit gate passed: fmt clean, clippy clean workspace-wide, 2881/2881 tests passed, rustdoc -D warnings clean.
description:
search_snippet.rs:30-39

  pub async fn search_snippet_get(
      &self,
      account_id: Option<&Id>,                       // ← unusual
      filter: serde_json::Value,
      thread_ids: Option<&[Id]>,
      email_ids: Option<&[Id]>,
  ) -> Result<serde_json::Value, jmap_base_client::ClientError> {
      let (api_url, session_account_id) = self.session_parts()?;
      let effective_account_id: &str =
          account_id.map(AsRef::as_ref).unwrap_or(session_account_id);

This is the ONLY method on SessionClient that allows the caller to override the session's bound account_id. Every other method (email_*, mailbox_*, thread_*, identity_*, email_submission_*, vacation_*) calls session_parts() and uses the returned account_id unconditionally.

Three contract questions the docstring (line 19-29) does not answer:

  1. WHY does search_snippet_get allow account_id override?
     The RFC 8621 §5.1 spec for SearchSnippet/get does not differ from
     other /get methods in this regard — every JMAP method takes
     accountId in its arguments. The override is not a spec-mandated
     feature; it is a design choice of this crate.

  2. WHEN should a caller pass Some(account_id) vs None?
     Per the JMAP threading model (RFC 8621 §1.4.2), an Email's account
     is determined by the mailbox it's in, and email_ids in SearchSnippet
     queries are scoped to ONE account. A caller searching across
     accounts cannot use this method to do so; they must construct
     separate SessionClients per account (since session.primary_account_id
     can only return one account per capability). So the override is
     useful only when:
     
     (a) The session has multiple accounts and SearchSnippet/get should
         target a non-primary one. But session_parts() always returns the
         primary, so the override is the only way to target a non-primary.

     (b) The caller wants to construct an ad-hoc account_id for testing
         or proxy scenarios.

  3. WHAT happens when account_id is None but session has no primary
     account for mail? Per session_parts() this returns
     ClientError::InvalidSession. The docstring doesn't surface this.

If the override is intentional, it should be intentional everywhere — every /get and /set method should allow account override for the same reason. If it's inconsistent because search_snippet was written first or last without revisiting the pattern, it should be removed for consistency.

Recommendation: pick one design and apply uniformly.

  Option A — drop the override on search_snippet_get for consistency:
    
    pub async fn search_snippet_get(
        &self,
        filter: ...,
        thread_ids: ...,
        email_ids: ...,
    ) -> Result<...>

  Option B — add the override to every method (or rather, add a public
  with_account_id method on SessionClient that returns a scoped variant):

    sc.with_account_id(non_primary_id).email_get(...)

  Option A is the minimal-surface fix. Option B is the "right" answer
  for multi-account scenarios but requires a design pass on SessionClient
  shape.

Cross-reference: JMAP-tjvm.22 (no public accessors for session/account_id) — option B is the natural follow-up if option B is chosen here.

Priority P2 because this is an inconsistency that callers WILL notice and ask about. Not a bug, but a contract gap.

Mark says NO HUMAN — Recommendation: option A (remove the override). The current override is not documented as a multi-account feature, and the design tension surfaced by question 2 above (one session = one account) means the override is not in fact useful for the obvious use case.
title: search_snippet_get takes account_id: Option<&Id> override — inconsistent with all other methods which derive from session
